If the discriminant is positive, there are two real roots. If zero, one real root. If negative, two complex roots. Use the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / (2a) to calculate the roots.

To find stationary points, take the derivative of the function f(x), denoted f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are potential stationary points. Plug each x-value back into the original function to find the corresponding y-values. To classify them as maxima, minima, or points of inflection, use the second derivative test.
